subject: Reserved capacity: traffic evidence & burst definitions
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@arborsystems.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-14T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Reserved capacity: traffic evidence & burst definitions

Hi Lina,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Arbor's product looks like a great fit for the reserved capacity plan we discussed. To finalize a sizing recommendation and a firm commit estimate, we need a short packet of traffic evidence from your side. Can you please provide the 7-day sample telemetry (CSV or JSON) that covers: average and peak concurrent sessions, request timestamps, prompt token lengths, response token lengths, and any session affinity markers?

To be specific, the items that materially change the GPU footprint for us are:
- Typical prompt length (tokens) and 95th percentile prompt length
- Typical response length (tokens) and 95th percentile response length
- Average concurrent sessions and 95th percentile concurrency across hourly windows
- Peak burst windows (we model bursts as contiguous minutes where QPS >= 3x baseline) and the duration of those bursts
- Session duration and KV-cache reuse estimate (what fraction of requests re-use a cached prefix)

If you have a CSV sample, a minimal schema that works for our sizing engine is: timestamp, session_id, prompt_tokens, response_tokens, latency_ms, cached_prefix_flag (0/1). Attaching an example template if useful.

We also need to confirm the target SLOs you expect under a reserved plan (p50/p95 token latency goals, maximum acceptable cold-start fallback behavior). If you can attach your internal SLA or list the expected p95 latency and any hard stop ceilings, that will help our placement.

If it's easier, send whatever telemetry you have and we'll translate it — just flag whether the sample is representative of a normal week or includes special events.

Thanks,
Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
[attachment stub: reserved_capacity_template.csv (csv)]

From: Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@arborsystems.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: eng-lead <eng-lead@arborsystems.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-15T09:30:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity: traffic evidence & burst definitions

Hi Rishi,

Thanks — attaching a 7-day sample (sanitized) as requested. Quick notes on the columns: timestamp is UTC, session_id is our internal session key, prompt_tokens/response_tokens are tokenized counts computed by our preprocessor, cached_prefix_flag is 1 when our frontend detected repeated context use.

Summary stats from the week:
- Median prompt length: 42 tokens, 95th: 180 tokens
- Median response length: 260 tokens, 95th: 1,200 tokens
- Median concurrency (per 1m window): 120 sessions, 95th concurrency: 860 sessions
- Biggest burst: on 2028-06-02 between 15:04-15:18 UTC, sustained 12 minutes, peak QPS ~4.8x baseline
- Typical session duration: 45s median, 95th: 6m
- Estimated KV-cache reuse: ~28% of requests show prefix reuse; reuse more common in short sessions

We also attach our internal SLA doc and a short note on the scheduled marketing event that produced the largest burst (to clarify representative vs. outlier).

Hope this helps — happy to jump on a quick call to walk through the CSV.

Best,
Lina Gomez
Head of Integrations
Arbor Systems
[attachment: arbor_7day_sample_telemetry.csv (csv)]
[attachment: arbor_sla_requirements.pdf (pdf)]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@arborsystems.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-15T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity: traffic evidence & burst definitions

Lina — great, thanks for the sample and the summary. A few clarifying points so our sizing matches real-world expectations:

1) Burst modeling: You indicated the 15:04-15:18 UTC spike was ~4.8x baseline for 12 minutes. For our burst-slotting logic we need to know whether you expect similar marketing-triggered bursts monthly (repeatable) or if that was a one-off. If repeatable, we'll recommend additional reserved burst pool slots.

2) Response tail: 95th response token of 1,200 is significant for GPU memory + token throughput. Can you confirm whether those long responses are full-generation (longform) or include attachments/embedded documents that inflate token counts? If those are rare (e.g., 0.2% of requests), we may route them to a separate larger-model lane rather than reserve all capacity for worst-case tokens.

3) KV-cache reuse: 28% reuse is helpful. Do you have a breakdown by endpoint type (search vs. chat vs. summarization)? Even a rough split (e.g., 60% chat, 30% search, 10% summary) helps our occupancy model.

4) SLA: you attached p95 latency goals — can you confirm whether the p95 target is measured end-to-end or after internal queuing? We size to end-to-end p95.

Action items for us: once we confirm those points we'll run a sizing simulation and share a recommended reserved-capacity configuration (GPU mix, burst pool sizing, recommended model quantization profile). Expect that draft within 48 hours after we get the clarifications.

Would you be available for a 30-minute sync tomorrow 10:00–11:00 PT? If so I can drop a calendar invite.

Cheers,
Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-16T08:00:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Reserved capacity: traffic evidence & burst definitions — next steps

Hey team — forwarding the sample and Lina's notes. Key sizing signals: median prompt 42 tokens / median response 260 tokens, 95th response 1,200 tokens, median concurrency 120 with 95th 860, a 12-minute ~4.8x marketing burst, and ~28% KV cache reuse.

My initial read:
- Baseline reserved pool to cover p95 sustained concurrency (~860 sessions) with worker autoscaling headroom.
- Recommend a small dedicated burst pool sized for the observed 4.8x for 15 minutes (we'll simulate with their CSV).
- Long 95th token responses likely justify a separate routing lane for big-generation requests rather than inflating baseline slot sizes.

Planned next steps (I will own):
1) Run the sizing sim against their CSV and produce GPU mix + monthly reserved estimate (48h).
2) Draft two fallback policies: route 95th+ token requests to a higher-memory model variant; and preemptive capacity expansion during scheduled marketing events.
3) Prepare a short SLA/placement note for legal billing on cold-start tolerances.

Camila / Marissa — can you review and flag any commercial constraints (min commit, pricing buckets) we should bake into the recommendation? I will attach the sim output and recommended commit in the follow-up.

Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
